summary: The root وَهَى primarily signifies weakness, feebleness, or becoming infirm.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.gloss: It was; became, much slit; rent

parts.t: said of a rope, (Mgh,) or other thing: or

headwords.def: وَهَى It was, or became, much slit, or rent. (Msb.) It was, or became, lax, flaccid, or flabby: (Msb:) or weak; said of a rope, (Mgh,) or other thing: or it fell. (Msb.) See وَاهٍ . وَهَِىَ It was, or became, uncompact, unsound, or weak. وَهَى أَمْرُهُ [ His affair, or case, was, or became, in a weak, or an unsound, state ]. (TA, art. نغض , &c.)

headwords.gloss: Lax; weak: frail; wanting in strength, compactness, firmness; toughness; unsubstantial; unsound

parts.t: Lax; weak: frail; wanting in strength, compactness, firmness,
See an ex. in the S, voce
, where it is applied to love, or affection.

headwords.def: وَاهٍ Lax; weak: frail; wanting in strength, compactness, firmness, or toughness; unsubstantial; unsound. See an ex. in the S, voce أُنْشُوطَةٌ , where it is applied to love, or affection. وَاهًا : see an ex. voce نُغْبَةٌ ; and see آهِ , in art. اوه , in two places.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
